summary: This informational document describes a PCE-based architecture for application-based network operations. Services like content distribution and inter-data-center connectivity need on-demand, application-specific reservation of network resources, and this lays out how a path computation element can support that.

eli5.summary: Some apps need the network to set aside a fast lane just for them. This describes a planner that can arrange it when asked.

subtitle: Architecture for applications to request on-demand network resources and services

tldr.problem: Applications like content distribution and data center operations need to dynamically reserve network bandwidth and paths, but traditional network management is manual and tied to specific technologies, preventing rapid service provisioning.
tldr.mechanism: Application-Based Network Operations (ABNO) uses a Path Computation Element (PCE) as a central coordinator that accepts service requests from applications, computes optimal paths, manages policies, and orchestrates provisioning across multiple network technologies and layers.
tldr.outcome: Enables operators to build responsive networks that adapt to application demands, working with existing MPLS, optical, and packet technologies while providing a unified control model.

facts.label: Provisioning methods
facts.value: Control plane signaling, OpenFlow, ForCES, NETCONF

today: RFC 7491 is an informational document describing a functional architecture and toolkit. It is not a protocol specification but rather a guide for how existing and future protocols fit together. The architecture has influenced SDN and network automation work, showing how traditional routing (PCE) integrates with newer programmatic control mechanisms.

sections.title: Application-Driven Network Demands
sections.content:
Modern networks integrate multiple technologies (IP/MPLS, optical, wireless) and face new demands from applications. Services like content delivery networks (CDNs), distributed databases, and inter-data-center connectivity need to reserve bandwidth and paths on demand, tailored to specific application requirements, across different network types and technologies. This is fundamentally different from traditional operations, where a human operator issues management commands to configure static services.

The Path Computation Element (PCE), originally designed for MPLS and GMPLS networks, can be extended to coordinate applications' network service requests. Application-Based Network Operations (ABNO) combines PCE with other components - databases, controllers, provisioning tools, and policy managers - to create a unified architecture that treats network resources as on-demand services. ABNO works with existing technologies and can be deployed as a distributed system or integrated into existing management platforms.
sections.eli5: Video streaming sites want the network to guarantee a fast path for popular videos. Databases want to spread data across data centers but need reliable connections. Instead of having an operator manually configure each connection, ABNO lets the application ask for what it needs and the PCE arranges it.

sections.title: ABNO Architecture and Components
sections.content:
The ABNO architecture is a functional architecture, not a software blueprint, which allows flexible implementation. Its core components include:

NMS/OSS (Network Management or Operations Support System) and Application Service Coordinator issue high-level service requests to the ABNO system. Policy Agent configures and enforces policies that govern how the network operates. ABNO Controller is the main gateway that receives requests, invokes the right components in sequence, and coordinates responses. PCE computes optimal paths based on network topology and constraints. Traffic Engineering Database (TED) holds network topology and capability information. LSP Database (LSP-DB) tracks established connections to enable optimization, protection, and restoration.

ALTO Server provides application-friendly abstracted network maps. Virtual Network Topology Manager (VNTM) sets up connections in lower-layer networks to create virtual links in upper-layer networks. Provisioning Manager issues commands to actually set up connections in the network. OAM Handler receives network alerts, correlates them, and triggers recovery actions. I2RS Client reads and writes routing state on network routers.
sections.eli5: The PCE is like a planner that knows the network map. The Controller is the receptionist who answers requests. The TED is the map, the LSP-DB is the notebook of what paths are already reserved, and the Provisioning Manager is the worker who tells routers what to do. The OAM Handler watches for problems and alerts the Controller.

sections.title: How Applications Request Services
sections.content:
An application or management system sends a service request to the ABNO Controller, specifying what connectivity it needs: source, destination, bandwidth, reliability, and any special requirements. The Controller queries the PCE, passing along relevant policies from the Policy Agent. The PCE examines the TED, checks the LSP-DB to see what resources are in use, and computes one or more paths that meet the constraints.

The Controller evaluates the PCE's response against application requirements and policies, then instructs the Provisioning Manager to set up the chosen path. The Provisioning Manager issues commands to the network - either to the control plane (asking it to set up MPLS LSPs or optical lightpaths) or directly to forwarding elements (using OpenFlow or ForCES). The TED and LSP-DB are updated as connections are provisioned. The OAM Handler monitors the provisioned path for faults and notifies the Controller if problems occur, enabling recovery actions.
sections.eli5: App asks, 'I need a path from here to there with 10 gigabits per second.' The Controller asks the PCE, 'Can you find a path?' The PCE looks at the map and says yes. The Controller tells the Provisioning Manager, 'Set it up.' The manager tells the routers. Then the OAM Handler watches the path and alerts if it breaks.

sections.title: Multi-Layer and Cross-Domain Use Cases
sections.content:
ABNO is particularly powerful in multi-layer networks, where lower-layer networks (e.g., optical) provide connections that appear as virtual links to upper-layer networks (e.g., packet). The VNTM works with PCEs at each layer to decide which upper-layer connections need lower-layer support, compute paths in lower-layer networks, and provision LSPs that create virtual topology in the upper layer.

Data center interconnection is a key use case: multiple data centers connected via a multi-layer network can use ABNO to establish reliable, high-bandwidth paths between them. Make-before-break procedures allow a new path to be set up and tested before the old one is torn down, enabling lossless service moves and reoptimization. Inter-AS connectivity uses multiple PCEs coordinating across Autonomous Systems to compute end-to-end paths. Global Concurrent Optimization (GCO) optimizes multiple LSPs together to pack them more efficiently or respond to failures.
sections.eli5: In a layered network, the optical layer (using light signals) supports the packet layer (using routers). ABNO can say, 'To route these packets, we need to set up a lightpath here,' and coordinate both layers. It can also reoptimize many paths at once, like moving trains on tracks to fit more through a bottleneck.

sections.title: Policy and Security in ABNO
sections.content:
Policy is central to ABNO. The Policy Agent receives directives from the NMS/OSS and enforces rules throughout the system, such as authorization (which applications can request which services), accounting (what resources were used), and constraints (clients cannot trigger unlimited server-layer allocation). The PCE acts as a Policy Enforcement Point, checking policies before computing paths. The VNTM and I2RS Client also enforce policies in their respective domains.

Security mechanisms include authentication and authorization for all requests, audit trails for all operations, encryption of control channels, and separation of concerns (an application cannot directly program forwarding elements; it must go through the ABNO Controller). The OAM Handler can detect unauthorized or anomalous activities and alert the operator. Different layers of the architecture can enforce different policies: the PCE might enforce path diversity requirements, the Provisioning Manager might enforce rate limits, and the Policy Agent might enforce tenant isolation.
sections.eli5: Just because an app asks for a path does not mean it gets one. The Policy Agent says, 'This app is authorized for up to 100 gigabits total.' The PCE respects that and will not give it more. Control channels are encrypted so adversaries cannot forge requests.
